title: Novatech - Procurement / MSA & DPA Review + SLAs
summary: Procurement call to run through MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, pricing approval process and onboarding steps. Customer emphasized SOC 2 and data residency, asked about private deployment options and uplift pricing for Dedicated capacity. Action items captured: send redlines, security pack, draft SOW and proposed pilot pricing.
next_steps: Samir to send procurement packet and redline summary by 2027-05-28
Maya to share security whitepaper and SOC2 report link by 2027-05-24
Schedule legal-only sync with Sara for week of 2027-05-31
Prepare pilot SOW and pricing worksheet for Priya by 2027-06-02
action_items: Samir Patel - Send procurement packet + MSA redlines summary to Priya - due 2027-05-28
Maya Lin - Share SOC2 report, pen test summary, and KMS integration docs - due 2027-05-24
Danielle Cruz - Draft onboarding timeline and support SOW for pilot - due 2027-06-02
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE on the Novatech account, with Maya our SE and Danielle on success. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Priya Raman: Hi Priya here, procurement.
[00:12] Jared Klein: Jared, head of security.
[00:14] Liam O'Neill: Liam, CTO.
[00:16] Sara Wu: Sara from legal.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Great, thanks. Goal today is to run through the MSA/DPA redlines you sent, cover SLA questions and pricing approvals so we can lock a pilot and onboarding plan. Maya, you want to lead technical on the DPA items?
[00:30] Maya Lin: Yeah, sure. I skimmed the redlines, looks like main asks are data residency, KMS for key management, and audit log retention. We support customer-managed KMS via our Private deployment or Dedicated with KMS integration, and audit logs can be exported to S3 or your SIEM for the retention window you need.
[00:48] Jared Klein: Two quick things - encryption at rest with CMKs is non negotiable for us, and we need 7 years of audit trails for a couple of our regulated customers. Does your retention and export meet that?
[01:02] Maya Lin: We can export logs indefinitely to your bucket; retention on the platform side is configurable but generally we'd rely on your long-term storage. If you need platform-side archival for 7 years we can discuss a paid retention addon.
[01:18] Priya Raman: From procurement side, legal wants to tighten the indemnity and termination clauses in the MSA, and they requested SLA credits for downtime over 5 9s. Also pricing: we need committed capacity pricing for Dedicated GPUs, and a breakdown of overage and burst pricing.
[01:36] Samir Patel: Understood. On SLAs: our standard is 99.9% for hosted, but for Dedicated we can discuss 99.95% on reserved pools with an enterprise SLA. Credits are typically pro-rata of fees for the impacted month, we can surface specific language in the SOW. On pricing, we have committed capacity tiers - Maya, do you want to take the pricing structure?
[01:54] Maya Lin: Sure. For Dedicated we tier based on GPU type and commit term. A 12-month commit gets X% discount, 24 months gets more. Burst into shared capacity is available at a higher per-token rate. For pilot we usually propose a small reserved pool plus burst for spikes, that lets you prove latency without a large upfront.
[02:15] Liam O'Neill: Is there any difference in model availability for Private vs Hosted? We have compliance customers and might need on-prem later.
[02:22] Maya Lin: Same model catalog across environments, though private on-prem sometimes restricts certain managed plugins. Performance and memory footprint differ a bit - we can provide performance profiles per model and a compatibility matrix.
[02:34] Sara Wu: On the DPA, we flagged the subprocessors list and want notification windows shortened for new subprocessors from 30 days to 15.
[02:43] Samir Patel: We can look at that; I need to confirm with legal ops, but we typically push for 30-day notice. For enterprise customers we sometimes agree to 15 with a mutual amendment.
[02:54] Priya Raman: Another ask is SSO. We need SAML + SCIM provisioning, and strict RBAC controls. Also we require SOC2 Type II and yearly pen test summaries.
[03:06] Maya Lin: We support SAML and SCIM; RBAC is role-based with custom roles for admin/ops/readonly. SOC2 Type II is available, and I'll share the report link and a redacted pen test summary after the call.
[03:18] Jared Klein: KMS integration - is HSM supported? Our compliance folks prefer HSM-backed keys.
[03:24] Maya Lin: Yep HSM-backed KMS via customer-managed keys in major cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For on-prem we can integrate with HSMs but it requires an ops engagement.
[03:36] Priya Raman: On pricing approvals - procurement needs a formal worksheet that maps committed GPU tiers to monthly fees, overage rates, and one-time onboarding fees. Also we may require net-60 payment terms depending on our internal approvals.
[03:50] Samir Patel: We can put together a pricing worksheet. Net-60 is something we can discuss with finance; typical terms are net-30 for pilot but enterprise deals often move to net-45 or net-60 with procurement approvals.
[04:02] Liam O'Neill: Performance benchmarks - we want a latency SLO for our workload (finance chatbots, 1k token context). Can you run a quick benchmark?
[04:10] Maya Lin: Yes, we can do a short benchmark with a model representative of your workload. For 1k tokens we typically recommend a model profile and a Dedicated pool. We'll need sample prompts and a test harness; we'll run it on a reserved instance.
[04:24] Priya Raman: Legal will want to see the MSA redline vs our suggested changes. Can you accept tracked redlines or should we send a marked-up Word?
[04:32] Sara Wu: We prefer Word with comments.
[04:34] Samir Patel: Word with comments is fine. We'll have our legal ops review and respond. Danielle, do we have an onboarding timeline template?
[04:42] Danielle Cruz: Yes - typical pilot onboarding is 2-4 weeks: kick-off, security review and KMS/SSO setup, benchmark run, iterate on prompts, then a production readiness checklist. For Dedicated, provisioning adds 1-2 weeks depending on capacity and approvals.
[04:58] Priya Raman: What about data residency? Some customers' data must remain in EU. Can you guarantee regional isolation?
[05:06] Maya Lin: In Hosted we have region pinning; for EU-only we can provision Dedicated capacity in eu-west with VPC isolation. Private on-prem also meets that but is more work. We'll document network/topology and prove with audit logs.
[05:18] Jared Klein: A few minor concerns: backup retention, deletion certs when contract ends, and role of subcontractors in maintenance windows.
[05:26] Maya Lin: Deletion certificates - we can provide a certificate of deletion for customer-managed storage and give an audit trail of deletion events. Maintenance windows and subcontractor roles are typically covered in the MSA; we can surface clearer language.
[05:39] Sara Wu: On indemnity we want limitation of liability higher for security breaches - is that something you can negotiate?
[05:46] Samir Patel: That tends to be a negotiation point; we can propose a higher cap for a tailored enterprise SOW. I'll get legal involved once we have the redlines.
[05:54] Samir Patel: Ok, quick recap: action items are Samir sends procurement packet and MSA redline responses, Maya shares SOC2/pen test and KMS docs, Danielle drafts SOW and onboarding timeline, and we schedule a legal-only review with Sara. Any other items?
[06:10] Priya Raman: That's it from procurement. Thanks.
[06:12] Liam O'Neill: Thanks everyone.
[06:14] Jared Klein: Thanks.
[06:16] Sara Wu: Bye.
[06:18] Samir Patel: We'll follow up with the docs this week. Thanks all.
notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcribes (e.g., Redwood Dedicated spelled various ways) typical of auto transcript. Links referenced to be sent: security whitepaper, SOC2 link, MSA redline pack, pricing worksheet, SOW template.
